Now I see the flow. When `newpkt == 0`, `free_packet(pkt, &parsectx)` is called at line 1658. But in `proc_plaintext`, `free_packet(pkt, NULL)` was already called at line 949. So the packet's contents are freed, and `pkt->pkt.generic` is set to NULL. Then at line 1658, `free_packet(pkt, &parsectx)` is called again. Let me check what happens when `pkt->pkt.generic` is NULL:

Looking at `free_packet` (line 414-486), if `pkt->pkt.generic` is NULL (line 416), it checks `parsectx` and returns. So the double-free is handled.

But the use-after-free is different. Let me look at the crash trace again: `proc_plaintext` -> `do_proc_packets` -> `proc_signature_packets`. The crash is "Heap-use-after-free READ 4". Let me look at what happens with the `c->list` after `proc_plaintext` frees the packet.

In `proc_plaintext`, at line 949, `free_packet(pkt, NULL)` is called. But `pkt` is the packet from the outer loop. The `c->list` nodes have their own copies of packets (via `new_kbnode(pkt)`). So freeing `pkt` shouldn't affect the list.
